correctness.rationale: A symmetric positive-definite harmonic drift and nonexpanding one-coordinate jumps contract coupled sample paths and yield unique stationary finite quadratic moments. The three generator equations are exact; their determinant is strictly positive for all allowed parameters. Cramer reconstruction gives the displayed polynomial torque numerator; factoring and differentiating the critical temperature ratio gives a globally positive derivative, establishing exactly one reversal iff the reset bath is hotter. The 347 exact rational cases corroborate rather than establish the universal identity. The proof separates potential torque from total reset-device work.

value.rationale: The natural problem is whether intermittent intervention can reverse the sign of the conservative torque of the archetypal two-temperature coupled Brownian machine. The result gives an entire sharp phase boundary, unique globally monotone stall threshold, necessity of hotter-coordinate intervention, and a nonzero universal high-reset torque limit. This is a complete physically motivated qualitative classification and parameter inversion, not an arbitrary parameter slice, repackaging of the no-reset result or a numerical sweep.
